news.full_article_text: Pope Leo returned to St Peter's Square on Wednesday for his weekly general audience - Published 1 hour ago Pope Leo XIV does not need any further treatment following an operation to remove a cancerous growth from his lung, his doctors have said. Test results on tissue removed during surgery confirmed he had had a lung adenocarcinoma, as was initially diagnosed, and that the disease was localised, according to a statement shared by the Vatican. "A subsequent oncological assessment has confirmed that no further treatment is necessary," it added. The 71-year-old was discharged from Rome's Gemelli Hospital over the weekend four days after his operation - stopping to speak to well-wishers as he left the grounds. It comes as he held his first weekly general audience since leaving hospital at St Peter's Square on Wednesday. The surgery, which took place on 13 October and lasted for 90 minutes, included the removal of the lower lobe of the Pope's right lung. The pontiff himself had announced during his weekly Sunday prayers that he would be having the procedure - telling those gathered in St Peter's Square that doctors had found a nodule on his lung. He said at the time that it had been caught "at an early stage". Images shared days after his operation, on Friday, showed the Pope celebrating Mass from the hospital wearing green vestments and standing behind a makeshift altar. On the same day, the Vatican said he spoke to Russian President Vladimir Putin over the phone to urge a ceasefire in the blockaded Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky to allow the delivery of food aid, and to call for "dialogue and peace". The pontiff had a similar phone call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday. news.full_article_text: Jeweller who crafted 'Sengol' installed in Parliament dies at 99. PM Modi condoles loss Ethiraj was the patriarch of the Vummidi family that owns 125-year-old Vummidi Bangaru Jewellers. India's leading jeweller Vummidi Ethiraj passed away in Chennai, on Wednesday at the age of 99. Following his demise, Vice President CP Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed deep sadness and condoled his death. PM Modi paid tribute to Ethiraj in a post on X, noting that he will always be remembered for his efforts in crafting the Sengol that was presented to former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. The PM said, "Deeply saddened by the passing of Thiru Vummidi Ethiraj Ji. Hailing from a distinguished family based in Tamil Nadu, he will always be remembered for his efforts in crafting the historic Sengol that was presented to Former Prime Minister Nehru." PM Modi said that many years later, in 2023, it was this government which had the honour of giving the 'Sengol' a place of pride in the new Parliament building. "Many years later, in 2023, it was our Government which had the honour of giving the Sengol a place of pride in the new Parliament building. During that time, I had the honour of meeting Thiru Vummidi Ethiraj Ji and expressing gratitude for what he has done for our nation and culture. His life and craftsmanship represent a remarkable connection between India's glorious traditions and our national journey. My heartfelt condolences to his family and admirers. Om Shanti," the prime minister added. "His invaluable contribution to preserving India’s rich tradition of jewellery craftsmanship leaves behind an enduring legacy. My heartfelt condolences to his family and loved ones," he added. Ethiraj was the patriarch of the Vummidi family that owns the 125-year-old Vummidi Bangaru Jewellers, according to news agency PTI . Ethiraj worked on the creation of Sengol, the gold-plated silver sceptre, symbolising the handover of power from British authorities to independent India in 1947. On the eve of Independence, Nehru received the Sengol from the Adheenams (priests) of the Thiruvaduthurai Adheenam (Mutt) in Tamil Nadu, who travelled specially for the occasion, the report added. Decades later, the Sengol found a place of prominence in the new Parliament building. Crafted by Vummidi Jewellers, the Sengol was ceremonially installed in the new Parliament building by Prime Minister Modi on May 28, 2023. news.story_lead: 'Don't meddle with powers of other agencies': Supreme Court to ED in case against Pinarayi Vijayan In a special sitting held during the Dussehra break, the Supreme Court allowed Vijayan and others to appeal against the single judge’s October 9 order. The Supreme Court on Wednesday stayed the investigation against former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter and son-in-law, among others, in the CMRL-Exalogic payoff case. It also reprimanded the Enforcement Directorate (ED), directing it to stay within its statutory limits and not meddle with powers of other agencies.
news.full_article_text: 'Don't meddle with powers of other agencies': Supreme Court to ED in case against Pinarayi Vijayan In a special sitting held during the Dussehra break, the Supreme Court allowed Vijayan and others to appeal against the single judge’s October 9 order. The Supreme Court on Wednesday stayed the investigation against former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter and son-in-law, among others, in the CMRL-Exalogic payoff case. It also reprimanded the Enforcement Directorate (ED), directing it to stay within its statutory limits and not meddle with powers of other agencies. “You (ED) have done your statutory duty. It is for the state to do its statutory duty. You have got a scheduled offence; you file a complaint and go ahead with your prosecution. Don’t extend your hands beyond the statutory limits. We are making it very clear. Don’t use your power to meddle with the statutory powers of other investigation agencies,” Justice Bagchi remarked when the ED defended the high court’s order. The top court stayed further investigation for seven days , allowing the petitioners to pursue their appeals against the Kerala High Court’s order directing the registration of a criminal case. Deep Dive In a special sitting held during the week-long Dussehra break, the Supreme Court allowed Vijayan and others to appeal against the single judge’s October 9 order. The court set aside the Kerala High Court division bench’s October 15 decision dismissing their appeal. The state had registered a first information report (FIR) on October 12 and was proceeding with the investigation. Also Read: HC order to file FIR passed without hearing me: Pinarayi Vijayan tells SC A bench comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said, “We direct the investigation in the FIR shall remain stayed for a week. Our order shall not be taken as an opinion expressed on the interim relief that the division bench (of the high court) shall fashion based on facts and the law.” The court clarified that the registration of the FIR had not been stayed; only further investigation had been halted. The high court had relied on a communication sent by the ED to the state police on September 22, disclosing a cognisable offence in the CMRL-Exalogic case. It was alleged that the state-owned CMRL paid more than ₹ 2.78 crore to Exalogic Solutions Pvt Ltd, a company wholly owned by Vijayan’s daughter, Veena T, without receiving any services in return. The payments were made by CMRL to Exalogic between 2017 and 2020. In January 2017, CMRL engaged Veena as an IT and marketing consultant on a retainership basis. However, tax assessments for the period from 2013-14 to 2019-20, submitted by CMRL, reportedly revealed additional payments to Exalogic for which no services had been rendered. Vijayan, represented by senior advocates Siddharth Luthra and N. Hariharan, submitted that the dismissal of his appeal had left him without an effective remedy. They argued that even the October 9 order directing the registration of an FIR and further investigation had been passed without hearing Vijayan. Luthra informed the court that, following the registration of the fresh FIR, the ED had filed a fresh Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR), alleging money laundering arising from the same set of allegations. In this connection, Vijayan had also been summoned by the ED for questioning on October 23. The bench observed, “Howsoever high you will be, you cannot be above law. We will not order a stay on the FIR. But on the points of whether cognisable offence is made out, the statutory requirement of continuation of investigation, we have said that you need to be heard by the high court.” The court left the ED’s proceedings untouched, stating, “We express no opinion on the validity of the fresh ECIR and leave it open to be agitated in an independent proceeding (by the petitioner).” The state’s actions also came under scrutiny, as the bench noted that the FIR had been registered on the basis of information shared by the ED rather than on the state’s own initiative. It referred to the statutory safeguards under the Prevention of Corruption Act, particularly Section 17A, which requires prior approval from the competent authority before an investigation can proceed against a public servant in circumstances covered by the provision. The Kerala government, represented by senior standing counsel Ramesh Babu, submitted that the information provided by the ED disclosed a cognisable offence, a finding also made in the single judge’s order. The bench said, “It needs to be ascertained whether information received from ED under section 66(2) is a mandate. The single judge goes flip-flop on this issue. We want the division bench to apply its mind.” Vijayan’s lawyers also argued that the high court had erred in entertaining a petition filed by advocate K. M. Shajahan, an outsider to the proceedings. Shajahan had approached the court two days after submitting a representation to the state seeking the registration of an FIR against the former chief minister and others. They questioned Shajahan’s standing to pursue the matter, particularly when the state had already constituted a nine-member special investigation team (SIT) to conduct a preliminary probe based on the ED’s information. Vijayan and the other petitioners further contended that the high court had issued directions for the registration of an FIR and an investigation without hearing them. Shajahan’s lawyer submitted that the law did not require potential accused persons to be heard before an FIR was registered. The bench referred to Section 175(4) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which replaced Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and introduced a requirement to hear a public servant before ordering an investigation into a complaint concerning acts allegedly committed in the discharge of official duties. Senior advocate Zoheb Hossain, appearing for the ED, argued that this protection applied only to acts performed in the discharge of official duties. The bench observed that whether the acts alleged in the present case fell within the scope of official duties was a matter to be decided on the merits. The court directed the petitioners to pursue their appeals before the high court including their prayer for interim relief in seeking protection from arrest. Vijayan stated in his plea there was no demand, acceptance, official act or money trail involved and the only link is the relationship with his daughter. He further stated that these allegations were dismissed in the past by the Kerala high court and Supreme Court in 2025. Besides Vijayan, even his daughter and son-in-law Mohammed Riyas PA and one Varish K had filed appeals against the HC order that was taken up for hearing on Wednesday. - Enforcement Directorate

It is not clear what specific proposals Witkoff brought to Putin, but Zelensky said after the talks that "strong" security guarantees for Ukraine and energy ceasefire proposals had been discussed. Putin's aide Yuri Ushakov said their ideas were not very "useful". Top officials from Russia, Ukraine and the US have held several rounds of talks aimed at ending the war. Russia blamed last month's "massive" Ukrainian strikes during its general elections for their disruption. Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory. The latest talks between Putin (right) and Witkoff lasted about three hours in St Petersburg Speaking to reporters after Wednesday's talks in St Petersburg, Ushakov suggested that a new round could be held around 10 November in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates. He stressed that the talks must focus on "building a security system for Russia and Ukraine after the end of the conflict." Ushakov also told reporters that Putin reiterated to Witkoff that Russian troops were advancing everywhere across the vast front line and had a "strategic initiative". Ukraine and its European allies have disputed Putin's claim, pointing to a virtual stalemate on the front. On Wednesday, Zelensky said he would accept a deal that would freeze the war along the current front line. "We call it 'ceasefire' or 'stop killings' like President Trump called it. Freeze and stop. And of course this is minimum what we need from Russia today," he told Fox News, adding that security guarantees for Ukraine could be discussed after this. Zelensky - and Ukraine's European allies - criticised Trump's move. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday rejected such accusations as "scandalous", and Zelensky said after the Oslo talks that intelligence sharing "works now" . Ukraine's military has also complained of speed restrictions to the US satellite internet network Starlink, which constricted its ability to use drones to conduct strikes against Russia. US officials have denied having requested such a slowdown and a bipartisan group of US senators has called for an urgent investigation . Hubbard had been in jail in Russia for allegedly fighting for Ukraine Before the Putin-Witkoff talks started, Russia released Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old American citizen who had been given a jail sentence of nearly seven years for allegedly fighting on behalf of Ukraine. Trump said the former teacher was "on his way back home" and "there was no 'swap' necessary", while Witkoff called Putin a "humanitarian" for agreeing the release. When asked by a BBC reporter whether he agreed with such a description of the Kremlin leader, US Vice-President JD Vance said: "I agree with Steve Witkoff saying something nice to a person who just released an American hostage. "Whether you agree with the underlying sentiment or not, Steve Witkoff is a diplomat. His job is to go over there and get a job done.
